_comments: Two negotiated deviations on CTR-900001 — what the app exists to record.
Both name a REAL provision of the 2026-02-02 Master Agreement, looked up by provision number, so
the standard clause renders beside the negotiated language exactly as D-16 intends. 9.1 is the
limitation of liability and 6.4 is expense reimbursement — the two clauses most often argued over,
which is also why they make the point on screen.
The provision lookup is scoped by template as well as number: provision numbers repeat across
agreement versions, so keying on the number alone would resolve to whichever row happened to be
found first and could silently attach a modification to the wrong edition's clause.
CTR-900001 already carries HasModifications = true. That is not redundant — the flag is asserted by
a person BEFORE the modifications are recorded (its job is to say 'go read the PDF'), and the shared
Validate() enforces only that rows imply the flag, never the reverse.

fields.ModificationText: Liability is capped at the total fees paid by Customer in the twenty-four (24) months preceding the act giving rise to liability, rather than twelve (12) months.
fields.Notes: Negotiated by legal; the customer's procurement policy requires a 24-month look-back.

fields.ModificationText: Prior written approval is required for any single expense exceeding $2,500 USD, rather than $750 USD.
fields.Notes: Raised threshold to reduce approval churn on routine travel.
